patterns.name: Invasion of Wind-Cold

sourcesChecked.document: references/course/LEC 02 Bleeding, chest Bi, Common cold.pdf
references/textbooks/Diagnosis in Chinese Medicine_ - Giovanni Maciocia CAc (Nanjing)(1).pdf

differences: The lecture core uses LU 7, LI 20, SI 7, BL 12, GB 20, and LI 4. Maciocia's Diagnosis pattern chapter uses the narrower set LU 7, BL 12 with cupping, and GV 16.
The lecture assigns cupping to BL 13 only when upper backache is present. Maciocia's Diagnosis and Foundations recommend cupping BL 12 as part of the core Wind-Cold treatment.
The lecture principle is 'Dispel Wind, dissipate Cold, resolve the exterior.' Foundations additionally emphasizes restoring the diffusing and descending of Lung Qi.
Foundations identifies LI 4, LU 7, and BL 12 with cupping as the main Wind-Cold points.
Deadman supports Release Exterior for LU 7, LI 4, BL 12, and GB 20. LI 20 is principally a local nose point. No textbook evidence reviewed supports assigning SI 7 a Release Exterior role.
The app currently has no pattern-specific clinical manifestations field, so textbook signs, tongue, and pulse are outside the agreed published-field audit.
decisions: Add GV 16 to the core prescription.
Do not add routine cupping to BL 12.
Keep the treatment principle as 'Dispel Wind, dissipate Cold, resolve the exterior.' without adding Lung Qi diffusing and descending language.
Assign pattern-specific roles as follows: LU 7, LI 4, BL 12, GB 20, and SI 7 = Release Exterior; LI 20 = local nose treatment.
Keep the existing additions unchanged: Yintang and Taiyang for headache, and BL 13 with cupping for upper backache.
